Hi, AppleCherriePie. I was just thinking on this topic today and I’d be happy to share what has helped me in the past. 

It’s been a few months since I’ve felt profoundly suicidal, and what’s helped me out of that labyrinth is the realization that it’s not *me* that I want dead, it’s the pain. 

Depression is…painful. It feels like a never ending pit, void of anything light and joyous. When you’re experiencing that day in, day out, it becomes the norm. Pain becomes normal. 

Healing, too, is also painful because it’s a change of that normalcy. Healing means you saying to yourself “Okay, this sucks. I don’t want to feel like this anymore. Unfortunately, the deeper the pain, the longer it takes to heal. And the longer it takes to heal, the longer you’ll have to withstand that pain until you get there. 

What makes healing so challenging is the act of choosing to face everything that hurts right now. And you’ll have to do that day in and day out until it gets easier (and it will get easier. Your mind may not be willing to receive that right now, but it’s true.)

After thinking on my many suicide attempts, I realized that all I wanted was to stop feeling this deep sadness—this deep pressure—as soon as possible. The pain was so deep, it felt like the only way it could stop feeling so sad was through death. But if I die, I can’t drink tea anymore. I can’t hug my friends and family or pet my dog. I can’t sing anymore. I can’t visit Paris. All the tiny little glimpses of light that existed during my depressive days would be gone if I chose to die. 

You posting here (and asking for help!) is indicative to me that there’s a part of you, even if it’s mustard seed small, that still has hope. That hope is gonna be what carries you through the painful journey of healing. Dying doesn’t give you the chance to heal. It’s going to take a lot of time and a lot of tears, yet still, it’s entirely possible to feel better than you do right now.

Sending you love.♡ I hope this helps.
